scope: Fix both findings from album-photo-alias-resume-rereview: adopt shared photo recovery on visibility restoration and defer bundled/local reader photo loading

fixes.finding: Resumed consumers keep an older failed photo after a peer recovered
fixes.implementation: On hidden-to-visible or background-to-resumed transitions, reconcile existing state with bounded successful-source metadata. Adopt a decoded success or a newer shared URI address using the normal provider key. Failure entries annotate actual decoded same-URL recovery without adding entries or extending lifetime. Late older errors cannot remove a newer successful source or invalidate a consumed recovery. Adoption starts with the recovered candidate and retains the remaining candidates for fallback.
verified: Two maintained consumers, one hidden, eight retry clicks on the visible peer: both photos appear after return with no remaining retry control
Both unchanged and changed download URLs recover across matching sources and differing URI/URL candidate lists
These four combinations sign three times and perform one rejected load plus one successful retry load; returning the second consumer adds no load/signing request
A resumed original that subsequently fails can still use its repaired preview
Unit invariants: newer rejections supersede older recovery; late old errors do not remove it; only matching URI metadata is accepted; recovery does not create entries or extend expiration

fixes.finding: The hidden live reader loads a new bundled cover photo
fixes.implementation: Gate local AssetEntity and bundled-photo provider creation through ActivePhoto, which follows TickerMode and app foreground state. Hidden children release their image widgets and resume lazily. Album frame/spine presentation and decode bounds are retained. Prepared print originals still bypass this gate.
verified: Actual AlbumReaderSinglePageView underneath an opaque Navigator route: updating bundled cover data and rotating starts zero additional asset loads while hidden; pop/resume returns ready photo pixels
Local browser AssetEntity photos, both page and spine rendering, perform no pixel decoding when initially hidden or backgrounded
All four local page/spine visibility cases resume, survive repeated visibility changes, and release tracked image handles after unmount/cache clearing
Bundled-reader tracking also releases all ui.Image handles, pending/live image entries and transient callbacks after closing

reviewed: Resume adoption is conditional on activity transitions, not scroll/build frames; at most three source candidates are checked, with no scan across the cache
Success metadata contains source/URL strings, primitive scope IDs and version tokens; no providers, pixels, contexts or widgets are stored globally
Existing success cache remains capped at 500, failure cache at 1000, URL metadata at 500; recovery tokens reuse failure slots and preserve their original age
Weak manager IDs remain collectible; stale failures and newer successful addresses are compared before invalidation/adoption
Same provider keys, memory/disk decode bounds, fixed reader texture budget and print originals are preserved
Every ActivePhoto lifecycle observer is removed in dispose; there are no polling timers or parked hidden-page futures
Restoring a successful fallback puts it first while keeping repaired alternatives reachable; the additional regression case verifies this

test_changes: Expanded test/review/photo_alias_resume_rereview_test.dart to cover matching/differing aliases, same/new URLs, hidden bundled rotation and resumed-original fallback
Added four actual local-photo visibility/resource cases in test/widget/local_photo_visibility_test.dart
Added recovery-generation, expiration/count and matching-URI recovery invariants to the two cache unit test files
limits: In-flight shared requests may complete while hidden; the change stops new hidden provider/signing work rather than cancelling another visible consumer's request.
Signatures/query parameters remain exact; success/rejection metadata respects the existing cache/decode scopes and URL expiration policy.
Tests use controlled signing, cache-manager transport and instrumented bundles with real Flutter image decoding, not live production services.
Handle/cache assertions and source review do not measure total native/device memory or frame time; physical-device profiling was not performed.
